quantity.quote: at a distance of 750 and 890 m from the reactors of the Palo Verde Nuclear Generating Station
The plant consists of three identical pressurized water reactors with a total thermal power of 11.63 GW
The 32 meter-waterequivalent overburden entirely eliminated any hadronic component of cosmic radiation
The segmented detector [2] consisted of 66 acrylic cells filled with 11.34 tons of Gd-loaded liquid scintillator

name: Palo Verde
notes: No official experiment website exists (the experiment ended in 2000); none recorded.

physics_goals.quote: We report on the initial results from a measurement of the anti-neutrino flux and spectrum at a distance of about 800 m from the three reactors
physics_goals.value: Search for electron-antineutrino disappearance at a distance of about 800 m from the three Palo Verde reactors with a segmented gadolinium-loaded scintillation detector

summary.plain: A detector in a shallow underground laboratory about 800 metres from the three reactors of the Palo Verde power station in Arizona. From 1998 to 2000 it looked for antineutrinos disappearing on the way from the reactors and, like CHOOZ, found no oscillation.
summary.technical: Long-baseline (750 m / 890 m) reactor anti-nu_e disappearance experiment: 66 acrylic cells with 11.34 t Gd-loaded liquid scintillator under 32 m.w.e. at the 11.63 GW_th Palo Verde station; data September 1998 - July 2000 (350 days). No oscillation: Delta m^2 > 1.1e-3 eV^2 at full mixing and sin^2(2 theta) > 0.17 at large Delta m^2 excluded at 90 % CL.
